preconditions.description: Attacker must hold some NOMOS tokens to initiate the attack
swapAndLiquifyEnabled must be true (default after presale)
Contract must have accumulated enough tokens in marketingAccumulator to trigger swapTokens function

violation_target.exploit_hint: Deploy a malicious contract that implements a reentrancy attack in its fallback/receive function. First, ensure the victim contract has accumulated marketing fees. Then call transfer() to the Uniswap pair, which will trigger swapTokens() in _transfer(). The swapTokensForEth() function will send ETH to the marketing address, but if the marketing address is your malicious contract, you can re-enter the transfer flow during the ETH transfer. Use the reentrancy to manipulate token balances before fees are deducted, allowing you to extract more tokens than you should be able to.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The NOMOS token contract has a reentrancy vulnerability in the swapTokens function. When marketing fees are swapped for ETH and sent to marketingAddress via transferToAddressETH, the ETH transfer triggers the receive() function of the marketing address. A malicious marketing address can re-enter the token contract during this transfer, potentially manipulating balances before fees are fully processed.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Deploy a malicious contract that will be set as the marketing address. 2. Impersonate the owner to change marketingAddress to our contract. 3. Accumulate marketing fees by making token transfers. 4. Trigger swapTokens by transferring to Uniswap pair. 5. In receive() function, re-enter the token contract to exploit the reentrancy.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Deploy ReentrancyExploit contract with receive() function. 2. Impersonate owner to set marketingAddress to our exploit contract. 3. Ensure swapAndLiquifyEnabled is true. 4. Accumulate marketing fees by making transfers. 5. Trigger swap by transferring to Uniswap pair. 6. In receive(), re-enter with another transfer to manipulate balances.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has a reentrancy vulnerability in the swapTokens function. When marketing fees are swapped for ETH and sent to marketingAddress via transferToAddressETH, the ETH transfer triggers the receive() function. However, the .transfer() call only provides 2300 gas, limiting reentrancy possibilities. The simpler exploit is to become the marketing address and receive ETH from accumulated marketing fees when swapAndLiquify is triggered.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate owner to set attacker as marketing address. 2. Enable swapAndLiquify. 3. Acquire NOMOS tokens. 4. Make transfers to accumulate marketing fees in contract. 5. Trigger swap by transferring to Uniswap pair when contract has enough tokens. 6. Receive ETH as marketing address.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address and impersonate to set marketingAddress to attacker. 2. Enable swapAndLiquifyEnabled. 3. Use deal() to give attacker NOMOS tokens. 4. Make sell transfers to pair to accumulate marketing fees (14% fee on sells). 5. Ensure transfers trigger swapAndLiquify when contract balance >= minimumTokensBeforeSwap. 6. Receive ETH from marketing fee conversion.
